pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/387

I'm not convinced:
- `sanitizeUrl` is already done in [`find-my-way`](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/master/index.js#L378)
- Because of encapsulation, `undefined` is used as default.

Suggestions?
pr_comments:
@delvedor the raw request has as `url` the url not the path. The query string is included there! 

I'd like to have the path in the fastify request object without the query string

Yeah, what I mean is, can you show me a use case where you really need it?
If you are inside a route you already know what is the path of that route, even if is dynamic.

I think for this case would be better a plugin, so we not need to parse the url two times for every request.

Something like
```js
fastify.decorateRequest('url', '')
fastify.addHook('preHandler', (request, reply) => {
  request.url = sanitizeUrl(request.req)
})
```
IMHO we should expose the sanitized URL somewhere.

> IMHO we should expose the sanitized URL somewhere.

Can you show me an use case?
The unique place where you will need it is inside the `preHandler` hook, because inside the route handler already you know the url.

Again, I think this could nicely fit in a plugin.

> Again, I think this could nicely fit in a plugin.

It's ok for me
I'm closing this, but we should definitely re-evaluate it in the future.

issue_context.title: Add path url to Request object
comments: I think the path and all such components (query string, anchor) should be available as properties of the object. See #393 for an example of why.

I think that this would fit nicely in a plugin, a decorator that adds to the request `url`, `querystring` and `anchor` and an hook to get that data.

Fastify is built to be super lightweight and extensible via its plugin system, in core we should support all the basic functionalities and the apis for the plugin system.
But these are core pieces of information that a plugin would want to use.

If a plugin needs this data, it can register the `fastify-url-data` plugin itself ;)
Again, I don't think this should be a core provided thing.

But since there are different opinions, we can vote!
Put a 👍  if you want this feature in core, put a 👎  if you want this feature as external plugin *(in this comment)*.

cc @mcollina @allevo

Let's not forget that add this feature in core would mean run some code to extract the "clean" `url`, the `anchor` and the `querystring` and add them to the `request` object for every request, even if you do not need that data.

IMHO everything that is not mandatory should be supported as plugin.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/handleRequest.js#L14

At least part of this information is already being parsed on every request. The suggestion is to go ahead and cache that data upon the first parsing of it. By shifting it into a plugin, this information will be parsed _multiple_ times per request.

I think we are already doing most of this for every request anyway (url in find-my-way). Parsing the anchor or the querystring can be done via accessors on first use.
We might have to refactor find-my-way to expose that data and avoid doing this twice.

I'm not convinced at all.

If the developers have not had that feature until now maybe it is not needed to keep this feature in the core

And a "communication/protocol" between `find-my-way` and `fastify` is dangerous.

So, `path` as another problem: plugin prefixes. Express does a lot of work in rewrite those for each prefixes.
Maybe we should not do them at all.
@jsumners that is a very expensive thing to do, I would avoid doing it for every request, bur rather do it on-demand with an accessor.

From `fastify` point of view, we don't need that feature: `fastify` engine (`avvio`, `find-my-way`, etc...) doesn't need this feature in order to work. So there's no reason to add it here.

I'm 👍  to add this feature on-demand and in a plugin.

I'd like to keep `fastify` as light as possible without features that aren't needed for the engine.
Closing this for now, but we should re-evaluate it in the future.
Does this solve the issue (and issue #388)? https://github.com/fastify/fastify-url-data
@jsumners looks nice, please release it to npm
It is now published under my npm profile. It'll get moved to the org when possible.
